title: Gluing supported cohomology in its lowest local degree
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum $k,\ell,E,n,A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $Z\hookrightarrow X$ closed, $a\in\mathbf Z$, and $d\geq0$. For a $k$-scheme $T$, let $A_T^{\mathrm{et}}(a)$ be the finite etale Tate sheaf of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], constructed using any power of $\ell$ annihilating $A$, and let $A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(a)$ be the pro-etale twist of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Supported cohomology means that of the underlying abelian sheaves [def-pur-support-cohomology]. On $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ put $F=A_X^{\mathrm{et}}(a)$, $C=R\underline\Gamma_Z(F)$, the right-derived sheaf kernel of restriction to the open complement, and $\mathcal H_Z^q(F)=\mathcal H^q(C)$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Suppose $\mathcal H_Z^q(F)=0$ for all $q<d$. Then for every etale $v:U\to X$, with $Z_U=Z\times_XU$, the canonical edge isomorphism
$$H^d_{Z_U}(U_{\mathrm{et}},A_U^{\mathrm{et}}(a))\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(U,\mathcal H_Z^d(F)|_U)$$
commutes with further etale restriction. Write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. There are canonical, pullback-compatible isomorphisms $\theta_{T,a}:\nu_T^*A_T^{\mathrm{et}}(a)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(a)$ for every integer $a$, extending [lem-amb-finite-tate-site-descent] by evaluation duality at negative $a$. For every such $U$, the canonical supported comparison (derived support applied to the comparison adjunction unit, followed by the direct-image comparison of [lem-pur-derived-support-comparison-direct-image] and then $\theta_{U,a}$) identifies $H^d_{Z_U}(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A_U^{\mathrm{pro}}(a))$ with the same sections. Consequently degree-$d$ supported classes on either site have unique gluing on every Zariski or etale covering of $X$. The vanishing hypothesis is essential; no such assertion is made in degrees above the first possible nonzero local-cohomology degree.

proof.text: Put $F=A_X^{\mathrm{et}}(a)$. By [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], $F|_U=A_U^{\mathrm{et}}(a)$ canonically for every etale $U\to X$, for all integers $a$. Set $P(G)=\ker(G\to j_*j^{-1}G)$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, where $j:X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$. Choose an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ in abelian sheaves. For an etale $v:U\to X$, restriction is exact and preserves injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] (with constant ring $\mathbf Z$). For an etale $W\to U$, both $(P(G)|_U)(W)$ and $P_{Z\times_XU}(G|_U)(W)$ are $\ker(G(W)\to G(W\setminus(Z\times_XW)))$. Thus the two support functors commute with restriction, and the restricted resolution shows $C|_U\simeq R P_{Z\times_XU}(F|_U)$. In particular its cohomology sheaves are $\mathcal H^q(C)|_U$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Also $\Gamma(U,P(I^\bullet)|_U)$ computes $H^*_{Z\times_XU}(U,F)$ by [def-pur-support-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support; Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic; Tag 015N, lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence

proof.text: For the closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, [lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction] identifies $P=i_*i^!_0$, with $i_*$ exact and left adjoint to $i^!_0$. By [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives], $i^!_0$ carries injective abelian sheaves on $X$ to injective abelian sheaves on $Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives] (constant ring $\mathbf Z$), $i_*$ carries the latter to injectives on $X$. Therefore $P$ carries injectives to injectives. This verifies the acyclicity condition for composing the sheaf support functor with sections; it is not inferred merely from the definition of supported cohomology.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support; Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic; Tag 015N, lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence

proof.text:
For a fixed etale $U\to X$, let $G_U(G)=\Gamma(U,G|_U)$. Abelian etale sheaves form a Grothendieck abelian category by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian], with constant ring $\mathbf Z$. Restriction preserves injectives [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives], so $R^pG_U(G)=H^p(U,G|_U)$. Step 2 implies $P(I)$ is $G_U$-acyclic for every injective $I$. Apply [thm-sp-grothendieck] to $(P,G_U)$ and $F$ to get the first-quadrant spectral sequence
$$E_2^{p,q}=H^p(U,\mathcal H^q(C)|_U)\ \Longrightarrow\ H^{p+q}_{Z\times_XU}(U,F).$$
Here $G_UP$ is exactly the kernel-of-restriction functor of [def-pur-support-cohomology], so the abutment is the specified supported group, not a different support construction. The theorem supplies convergence with the finite decreasing filtration in each total degree.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support; Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic; Tag 015N, lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence

proof.text:
By the hypothesis, $E_2^{p,q}=0$ for $0\leq q<d$. Derive the required filtration endpoints from [def-sp-convergence]: convergence gives $\operatorname{gr}^pH^d=E_\infty^{p,d-p}$ and a separated, exhaustive decreasing filtration. The graded pieces vanish for $p<0$ and $p>d$ by the first-quadrant condition. Thus all $F^pH^d$ with $p\leq0$ equal $F^0H^d$; exhaustiveness forces $F^0H^d=H^d$. Similarly all $F^pH^d$ with $p\geq d+1$ equal $F^{d+1}H^d$; separatedness forces $F^{d+1}H^d=0$. Apply [lem-pur-first-quadrant-lowest-row-edge] with $m=d$ to this finite filtration. It gives the canonical edge isomorphism
$$H^d_{Z\times_XU}(U,F|_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(U,\mathcal H^d(C)|_U)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal H_Z^d(F)|_U).$$
Indeed only $(0,d)$ can contribute in total degree $d$; outgoing differentials land below row $d$, and incoming ones start in negative columns.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support; Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic; Tag 015N, lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence

proof.text:
Use the single resolution $I^\bullet$ of Step 1 for every etale object $U$. By [lem-pc-grothendieck-edge-cocycle], the edge sends a cocycle of $\Gamma(U,P(I^\bullet)|_U)$ to its image under the sheaf morphism
$$\ker(P(I^d)\to P(I^{d+1}))\longrightarrow\mathcal H^d(P(I^\bullet)).$$
For a further etale map $V\to U$, evaluation of this same sheaf morphism on $V$ commutes with restriction from $U$. The edge maps therefore commute with every such restriction, as do their inverses. This proves the asserted naturality directly on cocycles, without assuming any additional functoriality in the second functor of the spectral sequence.

proof.text: First identify coefficients before comparing cohomology. For every $k$-scheme $T$, $\ell$ is invertible and $A$ is a finite ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$. Apply [lem-amb-finite-tate-site-descent] to obtain $\theta_{T,b}:\nu_T^*A_T^{\mathrm{et}}(b)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(b)$ for $b\geq0$, independently of the annihilating power and compatibly with scheme pullback. This is an assertion about ordinary finite constant-ring module sheaves. By [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], the module inverse image is the abelian-sheaf inverse image with its induced $A$-action; its coefficient unit is $A_{T_{\mathrm{proet}}}$. No change to condensed or completed coefficient categories is being made.

source.place: Tag 099R, section-comparison; Tag 03PK, section-kummer; finite-level identification as stated in lem-amb-finite-tate-site-descent

proof.text:
For $a=-b<0$, set $L=A_T^{\mathrm{et}}(b)$ and $L_p=A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(b)$. Both negative twists are the sheaf duals specified in [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] and [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Pull back the evaluation $L^\vee\otimes_A L\to A$ using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] and use $\theta_{T,b}$ from Step 6. By the definition of sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom], the resulting pairing defines
$$\theta_{T,-b}:\nu_T^*L^\vee\longrightarrow L_p^\vee.$$
On an etale cover trivializing $L$ (provided by the finite-twist lemma), its inverse-image pro-etale cover trivializes both lines. If $e$ is a frame, this map sends the pulled-back $e^\vee$ to the functional taking $\theta_{T,b}(e)$ to $1$; it is therefore the identity $A\to A$ in these frames. These local inverses glue: replacing $e$ by $ue$ replaces both dual frames by $u^{-1}$ times themselves. Thus the map is a canonical isomorphism. Pullback takes this formula to the same formula for the pulled-back frame, so the negative comparison commutes with every scheme pullback and evaluation, just as the positive comparison does. This is a direct local calculation for a line, not an assumption that arbitrary internal Hom commutes with inverse image.

proof.text: To use the on-route finite-module comparison with the abelian-sheaf support of Steps 1--5, apply [lem-pur-module-restriction-kernel-comparison] on both small sites, with the open monomorphism $T\setminus Z_T\to T$. Its statement identifies module-derived support, after forgetting scalars, with abelian-derived support; it also identifies the two short exact restriction-kernel models, hence their boundary maps. Ordinary evaluations agree by [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget], naturally in the object evaluated and compatibly with cohomology pullback. These are specified comparisons of derived functors, not an assertion that a module-injective sheaf is injective as an abelian sheaf. Use common universes containing the small sites and coefficients as these two lemmas require.

proof.text:
Choose a bounded-below injective $A$-module resolution $
u_X^*F	o J^ ullet$ using [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution-existence]; enough injectives is part of [lem-pur-module-restriction-kernel-comparison]. Exactness of $
u_X^*$ [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] and its module adjunction [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] imply, by [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives], that $B^ ullet=
u_{X,*}J^ ullet$ is termwise injective. The map $F	o B^ ullet$ represents the derived adjunction unit by [lem-pur-comparison-unit-injective-model], and is a quasi-isomorphism by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. Thus it is an etale injective resolution of $F$. Restrict $B^ ullet$ and $J^ ullet$ to every etale $U	o X$: they remain injective resolutions by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] and [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives]. These bounded-below injective complexes are K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. The pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] identifies the latter's coefficient with $
u_U^*(F|_U)$. The direct-image evaluation formula gives
$$B^ ullet(U)=J^ ullet(U),\qquad B^ ullet(O_U)=J^ ullet(O_U),\qquad O_U=U\setminus Z_U,$$
with identical differentials and restriction arrows. These equalities hold for all etale $U$, without a separatedness or finite-type assumption on $U$.

proof.text:
For every etale $U$, let $H_{U,Z_U}^{\mathrm{et}}=R\Gamma_{Z_U}(U_{\mathrm{et}},-)$. Define the canonical supported comparison by the explicit composite
$$c_U=b_{Z_U,\nu_U^*(F|_U)}\circ H_{U,Z_U}^{\mathrm{et}}(\eta_{F|_U}),$$
where $\eta$ is the unit of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] and $b$ is [lem-pur-derived-support-comparison-direct-image]. Both arrows are isomorphisms; this construction therefore works for arbitrary $U$. In the resolutions of Step 9 it is exactly the identity
$$\ker(B^\bullet(U)\to B^\bullet(O_U))=\ker(J^\bullet(U)\to J^\bullet(O_U)).$$
On every $W\to U$ the two direct images evaluate at $J^\bullet(W)$, and the restricted augmentation is the underived adjunction unit followed by the restricted resolution. Thus it represents $\eta_{F|_U}$ by [lem-pur-comparison-unit-injective-model], while the normalization of $b$ is that kernel identity. For separated finite-type $U$ (in particular $X$), this is the canonical comparison denoted $c^{Z_U}_{U,F|_U}$ in [lem-pur-support-site-comparison]. Thus the unit's on-route supported comparison is used, and its domain is not silently enlarged: the displayed construction supplies the additional objects. Step 8 identifies its underlying groups with the groups of the statement.

proof.text:
The boundary assertion on separated finite-type $U$ is precisely [lem-pur-support-comparison-boundary], applied to $F|_U$; its hypotheses hold on $X$. Here is the full check also for arbitrary etale $U$. By the injective-surjectivity assertion in [lem-pur-module-restriction-kernel-comparison], Step 9 gives identical degreewise short exact sequences
$$0\to\ker(B^\bullet(U)\to B^\bullet(O_U))\to B^\bullet(U)\to B^\bullet(O_U)\to0$$
and the sequence with $J^\bullet$ in place of $B^\bullet$. Their termwise identity is a morphism of short exact complexes. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality]; under [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] these are exactly the two support long exact sequences. Step 10 identifies the kernel component with $c_U$; the middle and last components are the ordinary comparisons $g_U$ and $g_{O_U}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology], by their adjunction-unit normalization. Explicitly, lift a cocycle on $O_U$ to a cochain on $U$; its differential is in the support kernel and represents the boundary. The same lift and differential occur in the other sequence, so
$$H^{q+1}(c_U)\partial_{\mathrm{et}}^q=\partial_{\mathrm{pro}}^q H^q(g_{O_U})$$
with the same sign. The module/abelian comparison of Step 8 preserves these short exact models. Thus the equality also holds for the abelian groups used here. This proves, rather than infers from a commuting square alone, the connecting-map compatibility on every allowed $U$.

proof.text: For a further etale map $V\to U$, all three maps between the complexes of Steps 9--11 are evaluations of the same restriction morphisms of $B^\bullet=\nu_{X,*}J^\bullet$ and $J^\bullet$. The direct-image formula [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] identifies them, so $c_U$ commutes with restriction to $V$. Steps 6--7 identify the coefficient $\nu_U^*(F|_U)$ with $A_U^{\mathrm{pro}}(a)$, compatibly with the same restrictions. Compose the inverse of this degree-$d$ supported comparison with the edge of Step 4. It identifies the pro-etale supported group with $\Gamma(U,\mathcal H_Z^d(F)|_U)$; Step 5 and the preceding equality give its naturality. This construction is valid also for $d=0$, since the identical-complex construction also applies in degree zero.

proof.text: Given an etale covering $\{U_i\to X\}$ and compatible degree-$d$ supported classes, Step 5 takes them to sections of the single abelian sheaf $\mathcal H^d(C)$ with equal restrictions on $U_i\times_XU_j$. The equalizer sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] gives a unique section on $X$. Its inverse image under the edge isomorphism for $U=X$ is the required global supported class; restriction compatibility ensures its restrictions are the original classes. Injectivity of the same isomorphism gives uniqueness. Zariski coverings are etale coverings, so the same proof applies to them. Step 12 gives the identical assertion for the pro-etale supported groups evaluated on these coverings. The argument uses the vanishing precisely in Step 4 and makes no assertion in higher degrees.
